source: DECISIONS.md W-29 allowlist, exactly (register v3 of 2026-10-19): (1) playbooks/music-sound.md DX-gated check ('not applied here' is body text about a broadcast anchor); (2) negations ('no co-keeper', 'Rings 1 and 2 are empty', 'there is no insider', 'Chhath is not hers', 'Minecraft is dropped', 'Minecraft was only an example'); (3) a 25 next to 'tested at 25, UNVERIFIED at 24' or 'access copy only if a 50 Hz venue judders'; (4) 'Ring 1' inside 'gathering 14'; (5) the P-class definition in playbooks/pushtimarg-world.md T1 (it defines P3, it does not permit it). Reviews and research notes are not entries: they are outside the scan (a historical record). Nothing else may be added by an implementor: a new entry is an orchestrator decision. Amended 2026-10-20 (week-2 close-out, on the orchestrator's instruction): entries AL-6a to AL-6e allow the history of the two retired phone figures '4 Mb/s' and '36 characters' (patterns W-29.phone-ph2-cap-4mbps and W-29.phone-caption-36-chars) in research fixtures, research notes, reviews, build/evidence and build/reports; only AL-6a suppresses a hit today (two research fixture lines), the other four are structural. Amended 2026-10-20 (week-2 close-out package w2t-t2-wording, d, on the orchestrator's instruction: Fable gate w2c r1, nudge 4): entry AL-7 allows the one phrase 'R8 pass mark scaled from 3,000 frames at 25 fps' in spikes/sp1_craft_cli/VERDICT-SP1A.md, where verdict.py now shows the 0.8.0 T2 envelope's mark text as recorded instead of rewording it at display time. The rows of AL-6a to AL-6e are S-66 since the same day, when the two phone patterns moved under the register's new row S-66 (scripts/stale_patterns.json).
how_it_works: A hit is allowed when its file matches 'file' (a glob under the repo root), its row is in 'rows', and context_regex matches somewhere in the hit's line and the 'window' lines before and after it. --audit-allowlist fails on any entry that suppresses nothing, except an entry marked "structural": true with a structural_reason, which is printed as 'unused by design' (it suppresses nothing on today's tree: its sample line no longer hits, or no scanned line carries the words yet; --self-test still proves the entry would suppress its own sample). An entry's 'file' is '*' (any file), a path, or a glob (* stops at a slash, ** crosses it); --self-test plants a glob entry's samples at a concrete path under the glob (reviews/** gets reviews/sample, research/*-fixtures/** gets research/x-fixtures/sample).
